Reading for writing · A love worth more than gold

lines.t: The story "The Gift of the Magi" begins with
endings in his stories. "The Gift of the Magi" is perhaps the most famous of all his works.
The story is about Della and Jim, a young couple with little money. Jim only makes $20
a week, and their flat alone costs $8 of that.
They have to worry about money every day.
Even though they're poor, Della and Jim each have one special treasure.
For Della, it is her beautiful hair.
For Jim, it is his gold watch.
It's Christmas Eve.
Della has tried hard to save money to buy Jim a gift.
It breaks her heart.
And so, she sells her hair to buy Jim a nice chain for his watch.
When Jim comes home, he is shocked.
Della's hair is gone!
At first, Della thinks he's angry with her,
but then she knows why.
Jim also brings Della a gift
an expensive set of combs for her hair.
How does he do it?
Well, here comes the O. Henry surprise. Jim has sold his watch!
The Gift of the Magi" is a warm story. In the end, Della and Jim have no money, and nothing
but the "useless" gifts for each other. But O. Henry does not invite us to laugh at the couple.
Instead, he writes at the end that "they are the wisest". They have something much more
they have love.

lines.t: Read the passage and find out whether plastic has made life better or worse.
When plastic was invented around the 1860s, it was considered an amazing material.
It was light,
It quickly replaced wood and other natural materials.
Many people believed plastic would make life better.
Back then, some people even saw plastic as an "environmental hero".
Not surprisingly, plastic has now filled our lives.
We can find it in bags, bottles,
and has thousands of uses. Despite all this, it has slowly and quietly
shown its dark side. Plastic waste was first seen in the oceans in the 1960s. Since then,
has become a danger to
more than 100,000 sea animals every year. By 2050, there could be even more plastic than
get tied in plastic lines. Bears' heads get stuck in plastic bins. Cows mistake plastic
a week. That's a whole bank card! Tiny pieces of plastic are found in the air
They can be carried around by the wind. There is even plastic "snow" at the North and South
Poles. On "Planet Plastic", there is no place free from this.
Plastic waste is hard to deal with. It may take hundreds of years to break down. Therefore,
hiding the waste in the ground doesn't solve the problem.
Burning it also produces thick smoke that causes air pollution.
Plastic makes life easier for many people, yet it brings long-lasting troubles to our planet.
Our choices today change the world tomorrow.
With no Planet B to turn to, we must think clearly and use plastic wisely.
